name: Component Firmware
description:
Adversaries may modify component firmware to persist on systems. Some adversaries may employ sophisticated means to compromise computer components and install malicious firmware that will execute adversary code outside of the operating system and main system firmware or BIOS. This technique may be similar to [System Firmware](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1542/001) but conducted upon other system components/devices that may not have the same capability or level of integrity checking.

Malicious component firmware could provide both a persistent level of access to systems despite potential typical failures to maintain access and hard disk re-images, as well as a way to evade host software-based defenses and integrity checks.

telemetry.name: Driver Load
telemetry.description: Loading of a driver into the running OS.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Sysmon DriverLoad (6) and retain image path, hash and signature result; distinguish load from file installation.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

sources.title: Apple Endpoint Security framework for macOS

telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and user: rare process/object combinations, bursts of object access or modification, and ordered parent/action sequences. Compare maintenance windows and signed software rollout activity.

telemetry.name: Firmware Modification
telemetry.description: Changes to firmware state or a firmware update observation on a device.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect approved OEM firmware inventory/update audit and compare version or measured hashes against a known baseline. Use read-only vendor-supported interfaces.

providers.name: osquery
providers.scope: Scheduled host-state queries; supported tables and privileges vary by OS. Select a table that actually exposes the required object.

providers.name: Linux Audit plus inventory snapshots
providers.scope: Events explain changes; snapshots describe state at collection time.

configuration: Define the inventory query, allowed host set, interval and least-privileged reader. Store a stable asset ID, observation time and collector version.
Keep successive snapshots and calculate additions, removals and changed attributes. Pair state changes with audit events when available.
Export collector health and missed-poll counts so a missing snapshot is not misclassified as a missing asset.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Snapshots miss short-lived objects and do not identify who caused a change. A generic inventory agent is not guaranteed to expose firmware or kernel-level details.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Compare authorized state snapshots: first-seen drivers/services/modules, unexpected configuration drift and integrity changes. Record collection cadence; absence in a sample is not evidence of deletion.

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for T1542.002 Pre-OS Boot: Component Firmware

analytics.name: Analytic 0916
analytics.guidance: Detection of anomalous driver and firmware interactions, including unsigned or unexpected firmware updates, driver loads linked to hardware components, and suspicious use of privileged APIs to read/write firmware or controller memory.

tuning.description: Environment-specific list of baseline firmware images for integrity comparison
Drivers approved for loading in production environments
Correlation period between firmware modification attempt and abnormal driver or process behavior

log_sources.name: firmware:integrity
log_sources.channel: Firmware integrity verification failures or mismatches against expected UEFI/firmware image baselines

analytics.name: Analytic 0917
analytics.guidance: Detection of suspicious use of ioctl/sysfs calls to access device firmware, unexpected flashing tools execution, and anomalous firmware checksums logged by SMART or kernel audit mechanisms.

tuning.description: Tolerance levels for SMART errors before triggering alerts

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: ioctl/write: Direct firmware update or device memory manipulation syscalls

log_sources.name: linux:syslog
log_sources.channel: Driver load events or firmware load failures for hardware devices

analytics.name: Analytic 0918
analytics.guidance: Detection of EFI/firmware manipulation attempts via abnormal driver loads, unsigned kexts, or tampered NVRAM variables associated with component firmware configuration.

tuning.description: List of trusted and signed kexts permitted in production systems
Known-clean EFI image hashes used for verification

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Firmware update events or kernel extension (kext) loads not signed by Apple

software.name: Cyclops Blink
software.description: [Cyclops Blink](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0687) has maintained persistence by patching legitimate device firmware when it is downloaded, including that of WatchGuard devices.(Citation: NCSC Cyclops Blink February 2022)

references.description: NCSC. (2022, February 23). Cyclops Blink Malware Analysis Report. Retrieved March 3, 2022.

actors.name: Equation
actors.description: [Equation](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0020) is known to have the capability to overwrite the firmware on hard drives from some manufacturers.(Citation: Kaspersky Equation QA)

references.description: Kaspersky Lab's Global Research and Analysis Team. (2015, February). Equation Group: Questions and Answers. Retrieved December 21, 2015.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.description: Perform regular firmware updates to mitigate risks of exploitation and/or abuse.

simulation.prerequisites: Use disposable lab hosts and test accounts, explicit target allowlists, a clean snapshot, bounded egress and a restore plan. Review every candidate and dependency before any execution.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
